chunks: And regarding the thigh, if it breaks and is set without a flaw or defect, its compensation is one-fifth of the wergild of the leg, being two hundred dinars. If it has a flaw, its compensation is three hundred and thirty-three dinars and one-third of a dinar, and that is one-third of the wergild of the soul. And the compensation for a fracture of the thigh is four-fifths of the compensation of its breaking, being one hundred and sixty dinars. If it was a wound that does not heal, its compensation is one-third of the compensation of its breaking, being sixty-six dinars and two-thirds of a dinar. And the compensation for its exposure is a quarter of the compensation of its breaking, being fifty dinars. And the compensation for the displacement of its bones is half the compensation of its breaking, being one hundred dinars. And the compensation for its piercing is a quarter of the compensation of its breaking, being one hundred and sixty dinars.
ai.seo_question: What is the financial compensation for a broken thigh according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This passage from al-Kafi elaborates on the detailed jurisprudence of *diyah* (blood money) for thigh bone injuries, reflecting the systematic approach of Shia scholars in quantifying bodily damages relative to the full wergild of the soul. It distinguishes between various degrees of injury severity, such as non-healing wounds (*qarha*) and bone displacement (*naql*), thereby providing a comprehensive legal framework for compensation in cases of physical harm.
